question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 44°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 23°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled ▵BDC, the remaining acute angle is ∠C = 90° − 44° = 46°.

By applying the exterior angle theorem on ▵AEC, the exterior angle ∠AEB equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

∠AEB = 23° + 46° = 69°.

**∴ The correct answer is 69°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In ▵ABC, BD ⊥ AC at D.

⇒ ∠DBC = 44°

⇒ ∠CAE = 23°

⇒ Point E is on the line segment BC.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the right-angled ▵BDC, the sum of internal angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠BDC + ∠DBC + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 90° + 44° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 134° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 180° − 134° = 46°

⇒ Now, consider ▵AEC. Since point E lies on the line segment BC, extending side CE to point B forms the exterior angle ∠AEB at vertex E.

⇒ According to the exterior angle theorem, the measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior opposite angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 23° + 46°

⇒ ∠AEB = 69°

**∴ The correct answer is 69°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is exactly equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Formula: ∠Exterior = ∠Int₁ + ∠Int₂.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°. This fundamental property applies uniformly across all types of triangles in planar geometry.

Right-Angled Triangle

In any right-angled triangle, the sum of the two acute angles is strictly 90°, as the right angle itself accounts for 90° out of the total 180° limit.
